 parts.append(f'\\n=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+text)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(parts))
print('\\n'.join(parts[:3]))

strengths: The broad audit addresses an important assumption in multilingual NLP: Wikipedia size and reputation do not guarantee useful training data. Document- and character-level statistics, together with concrete examples of contamination, placeholders, and repetition, provide a valuable empirical contribution.

The simple, model-agnostic pipeline and linked open-source toolkit offer practical utility. The correlation between MinHash removal and estimated bot prevalence (ρ = 0.63) supports the narrower claim that the procedure detects substantial repetitive content.

The experiments cover three training scenarios and several downstream tasks, with random-subset controls and five-run summaries for monolingual evaluations. Results such as Cebuano’s 12-point SIB200 improvement demonstrate that filtering can help particular languages.
weaknesses: The central identification of removed content with low quality is insufficiently validated. Appendix A explicitly removes foreign-script named entities and references, while the templatic articles in Table 1 contain distinct factual information. Redundancy, bot authorship, and script mixing do not themselves establish poor linguistic quality. A representative audit of retained and removed content is needed to estimate false positives and substantiate the claim that approximately 30% of documents are low quality.

The multilingual BELEBELE evaluation provides little evidence of preserved capability: Table 14 reports average accuracy of 0.25 for both conditions, matching four-choice chance performance; even English scores only 0.25–0.26. Small differences between these models cannot meaningfully validate filtering. This setup needs diagnosis and an evaluation with demonstrated task competence. The other multilingual result, XNLI, declines from 0.44 to 0.43 on average.

The experiments do not adequately isolate the proposed quality explanation. Appendix C trains different tokenizers for raw and filtered corpora, while fixed-epoch monolingual training and adaptation expose models to different numbers of tokens and optimization steps. The random control matches document counts, although deduplication disproportionately removes short articles, leaving token budgets uncontrolled. These comparisons support observations about the complete pipelines, but tokenizer, training-budget, and individual-filter controls are needed for stronger attribution.

The four-tier ranking and performance-preservation claims lack sufficient robustness analysis. The clustering follows several iterations and manual inspection without a reported stability analysis or justification for four tiers. DEPTH+ correlation is modest (ρ = 0.31), and length/entropy heuristics are indirect quality proxies. Similarly, treating differences within ±5 percentage points as negligible is not an equivalence test; Tables 12–14 omit uncertainty, and Acehnese loses 12 points in monolingual SIB200. Conclusions should more clearly reflect task-dependent benefits and losses.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the useful hyperparameter tables and toolkit link. The manuscript does not identify the Wikipedia snapshot and extraction pipeline, specify the MinHash shingling/hash/LSH configuration, or provide a reproducible clustering configuration. These details directly determine the headline removal statistics and quality tiers. Together with the validation concerns above, these are important revisions needed before a positive Findings recommendation.
